COLLABORATIVE_MANAGEMENT.eyebrow: The Approach Behind Everything We Do
COLLABORATIVE_MANAGEMENT.heading: Collaborative Management in Action
paragraphs: We believe healthy oceans can only be achieved when communities are at the heart of conservation. Collaborative management brings together local communities, government, scientists, businesses and conservation partners to share responsibility for protecting and sustainably managing marine resources. It is the foundation of everything we do.

Successful collaborative management requires more than protecting reefs or regulating fishing. It requires healthy ecosystems, sustainable fisheries, strong local governance, empowered communities, education and leadership, opportunities for women and youth, science and research, effective partnerships and, critically, sustainable financing. Our four programmes bring these elements together to create resilient coastal communities that can protect their marine environment, improve livelihoods and build a thriving blue economy.

intro: Healthy oceans are the foundation of thriving coastal communities. Oceans Alive works with communities, government, researchers and conservation partners to restore, protect and sustainably manage marine ecosystems along Kenya's coast.

We combine science, traditional knowledge and community stewardship to restore coral reefs, protect biodiversity, recover degraded habitats and strengthen the resilience of the ecosystems that coastal life depends on.

OUR_WORK_PROGRAMS.callout: Kuruwitu began as 30 hectares of protected reef in 2003. Today the model protects over 120 km² of ocean - proof that when ecosystems recover, everything downstream recovers with them.

intro: Healthy seas. Sustainable livelihoods. Sustainable finance. Oceans Alive works with fishing communities, Beach Management Units, government, the private sector and conservation partners to build fisheries that are environmentally sustainable, economically viable and locally governed.

We strengthen community fisheries management, improve governance and data, support Co-Managed and Joint Co-Managed Marine Areas, and help communities develop alternative and complementary sources of income - while developing sustainable finance models that fund marine management beyond traditional donor cycles.
workIncludes: Sustainable finance: CSR, concessions & payment for ecosystem services

quote.text: When fishers govern their own waters, the ocean responds.

intro: Strong, resilient communities are essential to successful collaborative management. Oceans Alive works alongside coastal communities to strengthen local leadership, improve livelihoods, empower women and vulnerable households, and build the capacity needed to manage natural resources sustainably.

Through our SHE Programme and community development initiatives, we support women and households to build sustainable enterprises, improve food security and diversify incomes - reducing pressure on vulnerable marine resources while strengthening governance, leadership and climate resilience.

intro: Education is at the heart of lasting conservation. Oceans Alive creates practical, hands-on learning experiences that connect people with marine ecosystems and build the knowledge, skills and leadership needed to become effective ocean stewards.

Through our Living Classroom, schools, universities, internships and youth programmes, we connect learning with real-world conservation - while our research and scientific monitoring ensures that local experience and evidence inform every decision we make.

OUR_WORK_PROGRAMS.callout: Every diver, teacher and researcher we train today is a reef guardian for the next twenty years. Conservation that isn't passed on doesn't last.
